hiddenCases.name: a different file gives a different answer
pandas does the reading
hiddenCases.describe: pd.read_csv rather than the answer typed in

exercise1.hint: pd.read_csv(path), then the mean of the score column, then round to two places. The second check swaps the file, so a typed-in answer fails.

questions.prompt: What does read_csv do with the first line of the file?
choices: Uses it as the column names
questions.explain: It is taken as the header by default. A file without one needs header=None, or the first row of data quietly becomes your column names.

questions.prompt: What is worth checking straight after read_csv?
questions.explain: How much came in, what pandas thinks each column is, and what the first rows look like. All three take one line and catch most import problems.

questions.prompt: read_csv guessed a numeric column as object. What is the likely cause?
choices: Some values are not numbers -- blanks, n/a, or stray text
The column has a bad name
questions.explain: One unparseable value in the column is enough. Finding which one is why you look at the distinct values before converting.
